summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted with coffee ground emesis and abdominal pain, two days after discharge from rehab for a gout flare. Evaluation revealed stable hemoglobin with a brief drop, leading to concern for a mild upper GI bleed. Imaging showed a large hiatal hernia with intrathoracic stomach and delayed gastric emptying, but no obstruction or diverticulitis. Endoscopy confirmed esophagitis as a likely source of bleeding. She was treated with IV pantoprazole, advanced to oral intake, and her symptoms improved. Acute kidney injury, likely pre-renal from reduced intake and contrast, resolved with hydration. Hypokalemia was corrected with supplementation. Her chronic thrombocytopenia remained stable. She was discharged home with plans for outpatient cardiac stress testing, surgical evaluation for hiatal hernia repair, and follow-up for kidney lesions and esophagitis.
problems: Diaphragmatic hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene
